Ongoing monitoring of both model accuracy *and* its impact on student agency is also crucial. Without those safeguards, my reservations would become objections.

A2.justification: While I appreciate the compromises made and the attempt to balance accuracy with ethical considerations, I remain concerned about the fundamental premise of proactively identifying ‘at-risk’ students. My support is conditional on a robust opt-out mechanism, ongoing monitoring for bias, and – crucially - a significant investment in universal support services accessible to *all* students. This model shouldn’t be implemented as a replacement for systemic improvements, but rather as one component of a broader wellbeing strategy. Without those safeguards, my reservations would escalate to outright objection.

A3.justification: While I appreciate the collaborative effort and agree with many aspects of this specification – particularly prioritizing fairness and limiting sensitive data usage – I remain concerned about the emphasis on predictive accuracy over student wellbeing. I would support implementation *only* if coupled with robust safeguards ensuring transparency, student agency (including opt-out), and regular ethical review.
